previous.evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc_scene_records, read-only analysis; already described as the property-bag parser by docs/SCENE_FILE_READER.md. __fastcall(Tokenizer* /*ECX*/, char allowUntypedValues, int parseGroupList). Optional '( name name ... )' group list, then '{'; the body loop reads a key, looks it up with 008f2260, and if the next token is '=' consumes it and runs the per-type read for the letter, otherwise recurses into a sub-bag only when the next token is '{' and silently drops the key when it is neither (008f6xxx else branch). Every typed read ends with BSP_SceneTokenizer_ExpectToken 008d9930 for the ';', which peeks and consumes only on a match, so a property authored without its terminator costs one reported error and consumes nothing further. That bounded read is what the reconstruction's value scan had to be corrected to; see docs/SCENE_FILE_READER.md Corrections. | CORRECTION, packet cc2_scene_property_bag: the ABI above is wrong. RET 0Ch is three stack arguments and ECX is the BAG, not the tokenizer: 008F5A25 copies ECX into EBX and spills it to [ESP+18h], from where it is reloaded as the this of every 008F3xxx setter (008F5D17, 008F6724) and of the recursive call at 008F6740, while 008F5A1E loads the tokenizer from the first stack argument into ESI for every 008D8xxx/008D9xxx call. So __thiscall(ScenePropertyBag* /*ECX*/, Tokenizer*, char allowUntypedNumbers, void* groupRegistry). Argument 3 is not a boolean: 008F5A47 loads it into EDI and 008F5AA9 calls 00469B60 on it to turn each name of the leading '( name name ... )' list into a bag, which 008F5AB3 then merges with keepExisting = 0, so that list is inheritance and a group's values overwrite. Argument 2 is the byte at [ESP+154h] that forces the I and F readers to read even when 008D8F10/008D8F40 say the next token is not a number. The twelve type codes, their letters, the eight reference sub-kinds and the 114h bag layout are in docs/SCENE_PROPERTY_BAG.md.
